            # Extra serial partitions supply CTAs when compute work alone cannot fill the machine.
            s = s + np.log2(f.output_tile_count_per_sm) * w[32]
            # Long-K makes the CTA-supply benefit large enough to overcome serial dependency cost.
            s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * long_k_gate * w[43]
            # Low-wave compute kernels jointly expose tail waste and poor CTA refill capacity.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 / (1.0 - np.clip(f.tail_waste, 0.0, 0.999999))) * f.wave_count_deficit * w[38]
            # Few tiles plus scarce residency prevent the remaining CTAs from hiding the tail.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 / (1.0 - np.clip(f.tail_waste, 0.0, 0.999999))) * f.resident_block_scarcity / (1.0 + np.log2(1.0 + f.output_tile_count_per_sm)) * w[39]
            # Compute-bound scarce surfaces need aspect-aware geometry rather than split-inclusive CTA count.
            s = s + f.tile_aspect_mismatch * (1.0 + p.output_aspect_imbalance) * spatial_scarcity * w[52]
            # Spatial tile supply directly exposes whether a geometry choice can occupy the machine.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + 1.0 / f.spatial_output_tiles_per_sm) * (1.0 + p.output_aspect_imbalance) * w[53]
        else:
            # Saturated compute execution has a distinct, more amortized wave/tail tradeoff.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 / (1.0 - np.clip(f.tail_waste, 0.0, 0.999999))) * w[21]
            s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[22]
            s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[23]
            # With sufficient output work, extra split-K CTAs are priced as scheduling overhead.
            s = s + np.log2(f.output_tile_count_per_sm) * w[33]
            # Once output work is abundant, serial split-K dependency is retained as a penalty.
            s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[45]
            # A tail combined with a wave deficit still hurts when compute is otherwise saturated.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 / (1.0 - np.clip(f.tail_waste, 0.0, 0.999999))) * f.wave_count_deficit * w[40]
            # CTA scarcity and limited remaining tile supply jointly amplify the final-wave cost.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 / (1.0 - np.clip(f.tail_waste, 0.0, 0.999999))) * f.resident_block_scarcity / (1.0 + np.log2(1.0 + f.output_tile_count_per_sm)) * w[41]
            # At abundant spatial coverage, compute-bound geometry follows output aspect and tile mismatch.
            s = s + f.tile_aspect_mismatch * (1.0 + p.output_aspect_imbalance) * (1.0 - spatial_scarcity) * w[54]
            # Keep spatial coverage separate from the split-inclusive scheduling term.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spatial_output_tiles_per_sm) * f.tile_aspect_mismatch * (1.0 + p.output_aspect_imbalance) * w[55]
    if p.log_flops >= 32.5 and p.output_work_per_sm < 234057:
        # split-K sweet spot: quadratic in log2(K-loop iterations per serial split), interior optimum
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count)) * w[58]
        s = s + np.square(np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count / (1.0 + f.serial_reduction_dependency * f.mainloop_iteration_count))) * w[59]
    if p.roofline_ratio >= 1 and p.output_work_per_sm > 200000:
        # large-grid branch (r09): CTA residency and register pressure on huge compute-bound grids
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[60] + f.register_file_pressure * w[61]
    return s
